newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKMA names top Mortgage Corp executives.
newsitem.headline: HKMA names top Mortgage Corp executives.

text.p: The Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation (HKMC) board has named four key management appointments to the territory's new Mortgage Corporation.
Leland Sun, previously senior managing director with Bear Stearns Asia, would be chief operating officer of the corporation, the HKMC said in a statement.
Philip Li, previously executive director of IBJ Asia, would manage the corporation's debt issuance programme and treasury operations, it said.

Pamela Lamoreaux, a director of international housing financial services with Fannie Mae, the largest mortgage corporation in the United States, was being seconded to the HKMC to work as a senior vice president, operations.
Lamoreaux had been acting as a consultant to the Mortgage Corporation project in Hong Kong since 1996, and would be in charge of operating systems and marketing, the HKMC said
Susie Cheung, a consultant with Deacons, Graham & Janes, was the corporation's general counsel, the HKMC said.

HKMC chairman Donald Tsang, said he was confident the new appointees would help the HKMC achieve its aim of "promoting banking and monetary stability, debt market development and home ownership in Hong Kong".
Tsang is also financial secretary of Hong Kong.
HKMC deputy chairman Joseph Yam said the team would lead the HKMC in the final and most critical stge of preparatory work before starting business in the final quarter of the year.

The HKMA, Hong Kong's de facto central bank, will run the Mortgage Corporation, which is aimed at easing the mismatch of funding between long-term lending and short-term borrowing and improve financing flows for home ownership.
